html:
Kelly Lake is a small Métis and First Nations community in northeastern British Columbia, close to the Alberta border south of Dawson Creek. The map shows its land in 1492, long before the community began.

Its founding families came in the 1800s: Métis fur trade workers, Cree, Beaver (Dane-zaa) and Haudenosaunee freemen from the east who had come west with the Hudson's Bay Company and North West Company. They trapped, hunted and kept horses on the edge of the Rocky Mountains. Related communities include the Mountain Métis and the Aseniwuche Winewak. See also Métis and Beaver.
